youtubeTitle: The Gospel and Soul Health Session 23 - Dr Bruce Wauchope
topic: Christ already in us: an unveiling
summary: Bruce identifies who the 'Christ in us' is: not one of many New Age 'christs' but Jesus, the only Anointed One, eternally one with the Spirit, in whom Trinity, humanity and creation are bound together in union. This Christ dwells in our darkness, and beneath everything in us are the 'everlasting arms'. Using Paul's Damascus road experience, he argues that salvation is an unveiling: God revealed His Son 'in' Paul, and scales fell from his eyes; Paul did not put Christ there. From Romans 10 he argues that the word of faith is proclaiming that Christ is already in people's mouth and heart, so confessing means coming to know a salvation that is already true. He closes with the story of an atheist patient who, after a shamanic healing went wrong, found peace and a loving presence within.
keyPoints: Jesus is 'the Christ', the only Anointed One: the Spirit is fully one with Him, and that oneness predates creation. He is not one 'christ' among many, as in New Age language.
To say 'Jesus Christ' is to say that Trinity, humanity and creation are not separated but bound together in union in Him; the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily in Him.
Christ chose to 'tabernacle' in our darkness rather than in some nice, tidy place within us.

'Underneath are the everlasting arms' (Deuteronomy 33): if you drop down through yourself you may become aware of other spiritual entities, but you should keep going. At the bottom is Christ, who holds all things together, and there is nothing deeper.
Paul's Damascus road conversion was an unveiling: the light was around him and in him, and God 'revealed His Son in me' (Galatians 1:16). He found within himself the One he was trying to kill.
Paul's blindness and the scales falling from his eyes are literal for him and an allegory for the human race. We are blind, and the scales must fall from our eyes and hearts.
Paul's law-based, 'contract' religious frame led him to kill in good conscience. Meeting a living Being, not a better frame, shattered that frame, and it took him three years to work it through.

You cannot ask Jesus into your heart because He is already there. Those who 'asked Him in' experienced an awakening to what was already true. This gives security, because you cannot take Him out and it does not depend on you.
A gospel that depends on what people must do offers nothing to the weak, the brain-injured and the 'incurable'. If Christ is in them, He Himself can proclaim, and there is hope.
Romans 10 does not start from separation: the Word is already near you, in your mouth and in your heart. Confessing does not cause salvation; it is how you come to know it.

Paul was sent 'to open their eyes' (Acts 26:18) so that people turn from darkness and receive forgiveness already given. The task is to proclaim Christ in people, not to move them from an 'out-basket' to an 'in-basket'.
Our love of family, of food and of everything good is the life (zoe) of Father, Son and Spirit flowing through us; 'there's more going on in your life than you realize.'

keyTerms.definition: Becoming aware of what is already true, that Christ is in us, rather than causing it to happen by putting Him there.
Jesus as the only one the Holy Spirit is fully one with, from before creation; the uncreated Son through whom all things were made and are sustained.
The binding together of Trinity, humanity and creation in the person of Jesus Christ.
Christ at the deepest level of a person, holding them together beneath their darkness and beneath any other spiritual presence.
Law-based religious frameworks, like Saul's, that can justify harm while feeling righteous.
Properly, the proclamation that Christ the Word is already near you, in your mouth and heart.
The divine life of Father, Son and Spirit passing through human beings in every good love and desire.

quotes: You don't put Jesus into you; you find Him there.
If you drop right through yourself you'll meet the everlasting arms.
He discovers in him the One he's trying to kill.
You can't ask Him in. He is there.

diagram.title: From Blindness to Awareness: The Unveiling

nodes.label: Christ already within
nodes.detail: Jesus dwells in every person, even in their darkness, holding them together.

nodes.label: Blindness and scales
nodes.detail: Religious frames and darkness keep us from seeing who is in us.

nodes.label: Proclamation
nodes.detail: Someone announces that Christ is in your mouth and heart.

nodes.label: Resonance and unveiling
nodes.detail: The Word within resonates and the scales fall from our eyes and heart.

nodes.label: Confession: knowing salvation
nodes.detail: We say and come to know what is already true.

nodes.label: Participation and growth
nodes.detail: We move with love, receive forgiveness and grow up into Christ.

diagram.note: Salvation here is revelation, not relocation: Christ is present from the start, and the process is about our eyes being opened, not about moving Him in.

caseStudy.title: Did my prayer 'work'?
caseStudy.scenario: Mia, 34, prayed to 'ask Jesus into her heart' at a youth camp. Since then she has worried that it did not take, because she did not feel much and still struggles with anxiety and anger. In bad seasons she prays the prayer again 'just to be sure' and checks how strongly she believes. Her faith feels like a test she keeps failing.
caseStudy.analysis: Mia's faith rests on a separation model: Christ is outside until she gets Him in, so everything depends on her performance and her 'believer meter'. Bruce's teaching reverses this. Christ was always in her, so her camp prayer was a real moment of unveiling, not the cause of His presence. Her security does not rest on how strongly she believes, because she cannot take Him out.
pathway: Honour the camp experience as an awakening to Christ already in her, not a transaction that might have failed.
Meditate on Galatians 1:16 and Romans 10:8 ('the Word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart').
When anxiety rises, picture dropping beneath it to the 'everlasting arms' rather than testing her belief.
Notice the everyday good loves in her life as Christ's life moving through her.
Talk with a trusted pastor or counsellor about the anxiety and anger, and seek professional help if they continue.

practices.name: Dropping to the everlasting arms
practices.how: Sit quietly and notice the layers of feeling in your body, letting yourself 'drop' beneath each one without stopping halfway. Rest in the truth that underneath are the everlasting arms holding you.

practices.name: Tracing the zoe
practices.how: At the end of the day, list three good loves or desires you felt, for family, food, beauty or others. Thank Father, Son and Spirit for living them through you.

practices.name: Proclaiming, not persuading
practices.how: When you encourage someone, tell them who is already in them ('Christ is in you and holding you') rather than telling them what they must do to get Him.

reflection: Have I thought of my faith as getting Christ in or as discovering He is already there, and how does each feel?
What 'scales' or religious frames might keep me from seeing Christ in myself or in someone I find hard to love?
Where do I see the life of Father, Son and Spirit flowing through my ordinary loves this week?

quiz.q: According to Bruce, what happened to Paul on the Damascus road?
options: He invited Christ into his heart
God revealed His Son in him, and he discovered Christ already there
He earned salvation through zeal for the law
He received a new moral code to follow
quiz.explain: Galatians 1:16 says God revealed His Son 'in me'; it was an unveiling, not an insertion.

quiz.q: How does Bruce read 'you will be saved' in Romans 10:9?
options: Confession causes God to save you
Salvation is only for Word of Faith believers
You will come to know a salvation that is already given
Salvation must be repeated whenever you sin
quiz.explain: He says it is 'not causality'; you come to know and become aware of salvation.

quiz.q: What does Bruce advise if, while turning inward, you become aware of other spiritual entities?
options: Keep dropping until you reach the everlasting arms, Christ
Avoid any inward reflection at all
Treat them as aspects of Christ
quiz.explain: There is nothing deeper than Christ, so keep going to the bottom; stopping halfway confuses.
